source.title: A Tail-Index Analysis of Stochastic Gradient Noise in Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Umut Simsekli; Levent Sagun; M. Gürbüzbalaban

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies minibatch size and network width and reports training and test accuracy, but its primary measurement is gradient-noise tail index rather than the generalization gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports tail-index measurements and a width-sweep accuracy figure. Tail-index results do not measure the claim versions' named outcomes. It also explicitly states that train and test accuracies were the same for different minibatch sizes.
record.test_reason: The AlexNet width sweep reports training and test accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, extending V2's width question to convolutional networks. The batch-size comparison does not establish V5's required fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete: the authors find heavy-tailed, non-Gaussian gradient noise and little effect of minibatch size on its tail index, and propose a Lévy-driven description of SGD connecting these findings to theoretical preferences for wide minima. They leave discrete-time behavior and extensions to degenerate minima unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates gradient-noise tail indices while varying architecture, network size, and minibatch size; it does not reproduce the original studies' generalization interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Tail index varies with architecture, network size, and dataset; increasing minibatch size has little impact on tail index. The authors report no significant differences across the two loss functions or three initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: FCNs reportedly reach the same training and test accuracies across minibatch sizes under a training-accuracy stopping rule or iteration cap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-size changes can preserve final accuracy under this stopping protocol; this does not establish equal-epoch performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient-noise tail indices are strongly non-Gaussian and change little with minibatch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD gradient noise can remain heavy-tailed across minibatch sizes. Tail index does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its correlation with generalization gaps.

record.problems: Accuracy comparisons across minibatch sizes are stated without numerical values or uncertainty. Width-sweep accuracy values are available only in a figure, and the text gives no precise comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
The specified one-hidden-layer ReLU setting on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; the reported accuracy sweep instead uses AlexNet.
Comparative test error of convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Large-batch performance under equal epoch budgets and the effects of longer training or adapted recipes.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized examples and comparing retraining accuracy with random removal.

missing.what: Recover width-specific training and test accuracies separately for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, identifying where training accuracy reaches 100% and how test error changes at larger widths. R2 currently records no readable values, preventing a verdict.
missing.locator: Figure 5; Section 3 stopping protocol; Section 4, Effect of varying network size

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. No verdict is justified from the available width-accuracy values. The paper's discussion of wide minima does not itself test V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.

The width sweep reports similar accuracies for sufficiently large network sizes, but does not establish the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU setting, zero training error, or continued decreases in test error beyond interpolation.
The study does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks' test errors under the specified conditions.
Adaptive optimizers and their held-out performance are not compared.
The study does not test fixed-epoch penalties against smaller-batch baselines, longer training, or recipe adaptations such as warmup or normalization changes.
Dropout and weight-decay effects are not tested.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap are not measured.
Memorized-example removal and retraining are not tested.

rows.subject: FCN
rows.size_stated: Widths 128, 256, 512, and 1024 are shown for the batch-size sweep; depths 2 and 4.
rows.operation_detail: Varied minibatch size from 1 to full batch and monitored accuracy.

conditions.value: not stated for this accuracy comparison

rows.value: same test accuracies for different minibatch sizes
rows.locator: Section 4, Effect of the minibatch size; Figure 6 discussion
rows.note: The authors state that they obtained the same train and test accuracies for different minibatch sizes; no numerical accuracies are given.
rows.check: Equal training and test accuracies across batch sizes are explicitly reported, but training stops at 100% training accuracy or an iteration limit. Equal epoch budgets are not established, so this cannot demonstrate absence of V5's penalty. Section 3 identifies MNIST and CIFAR-10 as the FCN datasets, although the batch-size paragraph does not identify which dataset Figure 6 uses.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.size_stated: Number of filters in each convolutional layer varied from 2 to 512.
rows.operation_detail: Varied convolutional network width and plotted train and test accuracy.
rows.note: The accompanying text says only sufficiently large sizes, which yield similar accuracies, are illustrated. This does not establish the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU setting or continued test-error decreases.
rows.check: Figure 5 reports the relevant width-dependent training and test accuracies, but its curves are not recoverable from the supplied text. The statement about selecting sufficiently large networks with similar accuracies does not establish the test-error trend beyond zero training error. The extracted partial state and plateau verdict are therefore unsupported.
